basis.historical_gap_resolved: The canonical note says production company discovery was not enabled. Current PERSONAL API and durable COMPANY_DISCOVER worker now execute PublicCompanyClient; the added tests verify that actual path and durable rejection.

criterion_ledger.observed_or_source_supported_reason: Mounted PERSONAL API rejects file, FTP, HTTP and scheme-relative URLs with 422 before any operation, DNS or socket. Production accepts HTTPS only; allowed HTTPS/TLS controls succeed.

Mounted API rejects empty authority, local names, credentials and private numeric literals. Client normalizes IDNA/case and requires exact origin. Independent TLS wrong-host and untrusted-certificate tests reject before HTTP.

Real worker executes robots and homepage over owned TLS. Homepage returns same-origin 302. Third real owned resolver process returns loopback; production raises DNS_PRIVATE before a third socket. Only /robots.txt and / are observed, exactly two vetted numeric connections. Existing unit tests also reject cross-origin, unsupported and missing-location redirects and enforce robots on the target.

Real worker rejects private IPv4 and IPv6 answers, including a mixed set containing several public answers followed by private IPv4, before any connection. Whole answer set is validated before address selection; existing cases cover an unsafe answer after nine public records and CGNAT/non-global classification.

Mounted API and real worker cover 127.0.0.1, ::1 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback. Native numeric resolver lookup separately returns public 8.8.8.8 and rejects 127.0.0.1 in the production parent validation.
API rejects IPv4 metadata/link-local and IPv6 link-local literals; real DNS worker rejects 169.254.169.254 and fe80::1 without a socket and preserves the blocked receipt.
file:///etc/passwd is rejected by the mounted API with 422 before queue creation, DNS or socket activity; the client supports only HTTPS and cannot pass a file URL to a network or file fetch.

API rejects HTTPS 80 and 8443; client origin permits only 443. The production resolver schema rejects a returned sockaddr using 80 even when the requested URL port is 443. Fixed-provider endpoints also have no content-selected port.

untrusted_content_boundary.production_path: PERSONAL mounted discovery API persists COMPANY_DISCOVER; workers.tasks constructs PublicCompanyClient. Candidate/homepage/career/sitemap/feed reads route through bounded_get with that client. Application-link samples preserve origin and use the same client. HTML/XML/JSON are parsed as data, not executed.
untrusted_content_boundary.tested_effect: All new worker cases inspect real persisted QUEUED/PUBLIC_HTTPS parameters, invoke execute_operation, observe the call-through original resolver raisingDNS_PRIVATE, and require BLOCKED outcomes. Reopened Store/API readback retains one completed attempt, zero retries, no next_attempt_at, no lease and MANUAL_REVIEW; terminal replay issues no new DNS or request and does not import jobs/sources or alter the profile.
untrusted_content_boundary.existing_content_tests: The two selected CompanyDiscoveryTests use a controlled fixture transport for unsafe/off-origin content and final-origin checks. Their assertions supplement, and do not substitute for, the new real PERSONAL-client tests.

reasoning: Company discovery enrolls only supported Greenhouse/Lever handoffs. Board-link parsing accepts exact supported HTTPS board hosts and bounded tenant grammar; authority tricks, foreign hosts and unexpected ports cannot become a provider endpoint.

Enrollment reconstructs API endpoints from constants and validated tenant identifiers. Registry factories receive provider/tenant/policy, not a page-controlled endpoint URL. Greenhouse detail identifiers are positive integers; Lever detail identifiers are UUIDs.

Shared provider request code uses follow_redirects=False and trust_env=False and rejects redirect responses. Provider-returned application URLs are validated/normalized as data rather than fetched by these adapters.

Under the requirement's untrusted-content-to-arbitrary-address threat boundary, attacker-controlled markup/job text cannot select a new provider host, port or redirect destination. This is a source-supported inference, reinforced by the independently executed provider cases.
fixed_provider_handoff.explicit_limitation: SourceTransport itself does not reject non-global DNS answers for these fixed trusted provider hosts. This review does not claim PublicCompanyClient-style DNS filtering or pinning parity for that transport, nor assurance against compromise of provider DNS/routing. Fixed destination allowlisting and certificate verification are the distinct safeguards here.

Two real owned HTTPS requests precede a same-origin redirect; a later private DNS answer is rejected before the redirected connection. TLS and HTTP parsing are real; a checked public numeric destination is explicitly mapped to the owned listener.
Fresh Store/API readback preserves the exact terminal receipt, one attempt, zero retries and replay idempotency. No job/source is imported and profile facts remain unchanged.
